protocol.py: 2 biology problems (1 error, 1 warning).

1. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A2 in slot 4: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 61:  p20.aspirate(2, reservoir["A2"].bottom(0.5))
   At line 61 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from water (well A2 in slot 4) with its tip 0.5
   mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 30 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well
   Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.19 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air. The
   simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from these
   draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A2 in slot 4.
   Also reached 1 other well: well H12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 111 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 0.5 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a
   tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot
   [d8d6f330c481]

2. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 95 stocks
   line 64:  p20.aspirate(2, src_well.bottom(0.5))
   At line 64 the tip went into sample_1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample_9 (well A2 in slot 2),
   sample_17 (well A3 in slot 2), sample_25 (well A4 in slot 2) and 91 more while it still
   carried master mix (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step (this line did it 95 times).
   A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so
   these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw
   from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer
   clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 87 more in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 64 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [257f4bbe021e]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A2 in slot 4: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 61 the p20_single_gen2 draws 2 ul from water (well A2 in slot 4) with its tip 0.5 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 30 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.19 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air. The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 1 well filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 111 ul in it for the surface to reach 0.5 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 95 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 64 the tip went into sample_1 (well A1 in slot 2), sample_9 (well A2 in slot 2), sample_17 (well A3 in slot 2), sample_25 (well A4 in slot 2) and 91 more while it still carried master mix (well A1 in slot 4) from an earlier step (this line did it 95 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 64 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.
